author: WP01
summary: Catalogues the three CNAEXT mechanisms, extension surfaces by area (framework/math, graphics/content, input/audio/media/host services), the graphics-ext engine layer and the strict compile check. Mostly current for d6e9ff05; stale at TARGET in the marker count, the engine-layer test count, morph-target tangent scope and a few member descriptions. The site covered the engine layer in depth and the mechanisms briefly; the per-namespace catalogue with real member names, the marker/suffix independence and the strict-check proof were missing and form the new CNAEXT catalogue page.

concepts.text: 'CNA extension' names three mechanisms: the CNAEXT declaration marker, the project-owned CNA::* namespaces, and the CNA_CNAEXT option with the CNA::CnaExt interface target composing graphics-ext and devices-ext.
The retired pre-rename target spelling survives only through compatibility wiring; current vocabulary is CNAEXT.

target.evidence: modules/CMakeLists.txt comment (named cna_noxna/CNA::NoXna before the 2026-08 normalisation)

concepts.text: A whole-token scan finds 2,904 CNAEXT occurrences across 406 headers, a count that moves with API classification.

target.evidence: At 009d40f5 under modules/*/include: 1,843 code tokens in 330 headers (comments stripped); 2,279 whole words in 353 headers including comments

concepts.text: GameWindow *EXT members give raw SDL window access, borderless state and minimize/restore.

target.evidence: GameWindow.hpp: the handle is a platform-neutral CNA::Platform::NativeWindowHandle; drag-and-drop events added; the borderless accessors are suffixed but unmarked

concepts.text: GraphicsDeviceManager presentation modes (letterbox, overscan, stretch, native back buffer, fixed-height/dynamic-width) layer scaling policy around XNA's manager.
Matrix::ToColumnMajor is an explicit bridge from row-vector storage to column-major uniform APIs.
Color gains byte-component construction and convenience operators absent from the reference surface.
GetTypeName implementations are a project-wide runtime type-name bridge from sharp-runtime conventions, not an XNA member family.
AsciiPostProcessEffect is a reusable quantisation/glyph-atlas effect recovered from a removed renderer identity and lives in graphics-ext as a renderer-neutral extension, not a renderer.
concepts.note: The Bible's 'not a 47th renderer' counts an old renderer total; the origin is not named here by policy.

concepts.text: PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect are metallic-roughness materials whose renderer coverage is capability- and test-qualified rather than implied by type presence.
AnimationPlayer and SkinningData are a runtime skeletal system derived from the historical XNA skinned-model sample, separate from the avatar SkinnedModelEXT system.
Morph-target *EXT surfaces blend CPU deltas with weights and animation through model tags, POSITION and NORMAL only, tangent deltas out of scope.
concepts.note: Tangent deltas are blended at TARGET (direction only, handedness kept from the base vertex).

concepts.text: ShaderEffect is the renderer-specific source/program custom-shader route and does not make a renderer support the separate compiled Effect Framework route.
tokens: does not make a renderer support the separate compiled-effect route

concepts.text: Texture and format helpers add raw pixel/data helpers, DDS cube loading, format-size queries and extra surface formats, whose presence does not mean support on every renderer.
Graphics diagnostics and recovery extensions cover string markers, context-loss simulation and recovery controls, screenshot/readback and headless hooks; hook presence and host evidence are separate.

target.evidence: GraphicsDevice.hpp (SetStringMarkerEXT, SetContextRecoveryEnabled, NotifyContentLostResourcesEXT); context-loss simulation is the internal IGraphicsRenderer::DebugSimulateContextLoss hook, not public API

concepts.text: The CNJ system (JSON envelope, typed loaders, offline model sidecars) is project-owned with reader-specific payloads, not a universal schema.
Content manifests and XNB usage summaries enumerate discovered assets and reader-name use for audits; introspection does not resolve or validate every asset.
The graphics extensions span the graphics, content and graphics-ext modules; directory ownership and public API classification are different axes.
tokens: directory ownership and API classification are different axes

concepts.text: graphics-ext is an engine-oriented layer over GraphicsDevice, not a renderer; its public CNA/Graphics directory has 98 headers and its test tree 91 C++ sources, counts of scope not execution.

target.evidence: At 009d40f5: 98 headers in modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics and 92 .cpp under modules/graphics-ext/tests

concepts.text: The layer's surfaces form six groups: materials and environments, lights and shadows, frame pipeline and post-processing, geometry scale, modern resources and observation.

The layer checks named capabilities at use sites; some algorithms keep an intentional CPU path (clustered assignment, with tests comparing CPU and GPU results) while others refuse by name; no silent substitute.

Engine-layer tests must be read by kind: arithmetic/grid/material tests with a recording device, shader-package freshness, resource interop needing an engaged renderer, and pixel-reaching visibility/shadow/post tests; application repositories add integrated observations at their own pins.
tokens: 92 test sources are not 92 renderer-qualified pixel suites

target.evidence: modules/graphics-ext/tests (Recording*Renderer doubles in four files); no workflow sets CNA_CNAEXT=ON

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: Input extensions add clipboard, joystick, power, haptics, scancode/key-name queries, mouse capture and global position, and modern gamepad identity, lights, trigger vibration and sensors beyond XNA's Xbox 360 model.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: DynamicSoundEffectInstance accepts float buffers, whereas real XNA's streaming surface accepts 16-bit PCM bytes only.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: Media adds video URI and audio/video track selection EXT methods; some originate in FNA extensions but remain outside original XNA.

target.evidence: Video.hpp, VideoPlayer.hpp; FNA@b3551247 src/Media/Video/Video.cs, VideoPlayer.cs (FromUriEXT, SetAudioTrackEXT, SetVideoTrackEXT)

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: CNA::Devices camera, dialogs, locale, URL, system, clipboard and power services live in the devices-ext module, distinct from Microsoft::Devices::Sensors.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: Sensors carry synthetic injection, state-symmetry and extra vibration/support helpers marked inside Microsoft-shaped classes, useful as testing and platform bridges.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: Storage adds application-name and storage-root helpers because CNA needs a deterministic local root where XNA chose a device through platform UI.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: GamerServices extensions add local overlay rendering and simulation, ranking re-pagination and persistence hooks, making local behaviour testable without claiming Xbox LIVE.

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: Networking adds public/internal setters and host-delivery controls needed by the ENet-backed implementation.

target.evidence: NetworkSession.hpp at TARGET: the marked members found are lifetime test counters and the Sender field; the setter description is not borne out

concepts.section: Input, audio, media, and host services
concepts.text: The marker says only 'not original XNA'; extension surface still needs ownership, failure, hostile-input and host-evidence analysis.

concepts.section: How the strict check proves itself
concepts.text: Two standalone harness directions give the marker force: a positive target compiling the intended XNA surface with the define and warnings-as-errors, and an excluded negative target that must fail, checked by an inverted CTest.

concepts.section: How the strict check proves itself
concepts.text: The pair proves acceptance and sensitivity for the exercised slice but not that every addition is marked; that still needs comparison with the reference surface.
